info.name: UniLantern Student Backend API
info.description:
Comprehensive Postman collection covering all 71 requests for the current UniLantern Backend API, updated from the Express routes and Zod schemas in src as of 2026-05-22.

Base URL: {{base_url}} (default: http://localhost:3000)

Auth quick start:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/student/otp/send with purpose signup or login.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/student/otp/verify and copy phone_verify_token from the response.
3. For signup, POST /api/v1/auth/student/signup with phone_verify_token and required profile fields. Signup creates the student profile row immediately.
4. For login, POST /api/v1/auth/student/login with phone_verify_token.
5. Store access_token and refresh_token for authenticated endpoints.

Readiness scoring is queued asynchronously after profile, academics, extracurricular, essay, awards, and service writes.

request.description:
Complete legacy signup with verified phone number. Returns access_token and refresh_token and creates the student_profiles row immediately.

Required fields:

- phone_number (E.164 format)
    
- otp_code (from OTP verify)
    
- email
    
- full_name
    
- graduation_year (integer)
    
- date_of_birth (YYYY-MM-DD)
    
- high_school_name
    
- state_of_residence
    
- confirms_age_13_plus (boolean, must be true)
    
- confirms_parental_permission (boolean, must be true)

Optional:

- grade (9-12)
Login with phone number and verified OTP code. Returns access_token and refresh_token.
Refresh the access token using refresh token. Call when access_token is about to expire.

Get essay status (NOT essay_text content). Shows status, word_count, locks, and finalization info.

body.raw:
{
  "essay_text": "One of the biggest challenges I ever faced happened during my second year of engineering college. I was selected to lead a group project for a technical competition, and at first I felt confident and excited. However, managing a team turned out to be much harder than I expected. Different members had different ideas, some people missed deadlines, and communication slowly became weaker. At the same time, I was also preparing for exams, which made the pressure even greater. Our first presentation went badly, and the judges pointed out several mistakes in our planning and teamwork.

After that failure, I realized I had two choices: either give up or improve myself. I decided to work harder and become more organized. I created proper schedules, divided tasks clearly, and encouraged open communication among the team members. I also learned how to listen carefully to other opinions instead of trying to control everything alone. Slowly, our teamwork improved, and everyone became more motivated.

By the final round, we presented our project with confidence and received positive feedback from the judges. This challenge taught me that leadership is not about perfection but about patience, teamwork, and learning from mistakes. Most importantly, I learned that difficult situations often help people discover strengths they never knew they had before.

Before this experience, I avoided responsibilities because I feared criticism and failure. After overcoming this challenge, I became more confident while speaking in front of others and participating in new activities. The lessons I learned continue to guide me in academics, teamwork, and growth every day.",
  "essay_prompt": "Describe a challenge you overcame and what you learned."
}
